item.description:
### Added - **Cursor is now a supported agent, alongside Claude Code and Codex.** Your Cursor sessions show up in the menu bar, on your iPhone and on your watch, the same as the other two: which project, what it's doing right now, and whether it's working or finished. Both the `cursor-agent` CLI and the Cursor app are covered by the same one-time setup. - Cursor sessions appear even if you started them before Perch was running, and clicking one jumps to the terminal it's in. - "Finished" notifications for Cursor turns, on the Mac and pushed to your phone. - Per-session token and context figures for Cursor. - Cursor in Stats — sessions, active days, streaks and the contribution heatmap, with its own filter next to Claude and Codex. - A "Cursor real-time integration" switch in Settings, on by default and a no-op if you don't have Cursor. It adds one entry to `~/.cursor/hooks.json`, leaves any hooks other tools put there untouched, and removes cleanly when switched off.
### Fixed - **Cursor sessions used to show up as Claude Code sessions that never did anything.** If you had Perch and Cursor both installed, Cursor was already quietly triggering Perch and creating a session that was labelled Claude Code, showed "default" as its model, and sat in its starting state forever no matter how much work Cursor did. Those rows are gone — Cursor sessions are now reported as Cursor sessions, correctly. - `scripts/uninstall.sh` now removes Perch's Codex and Cursor hooks as well as its Claude Code ones. It previously left them behind, so uninstalling with `--app` deleted the programs those hooks pointed at and left the agents running a command that no longer existed.
### Note - **Cursor has no Allow/Deny in Perch, deliberately.** Cursor's approval hook fires before *every* shell command, not only the ones it was going to ask you about — so wiring it up would turn routine, already-approved commands into lock-screen prompts on your phone. Cursor sessions therefore never show "Needs you"; approvals stay in Cursor itself. Claude Code and Codex are unchanged. - Perch shows no cost estimate for Cursor sessions yet, and Cursor contributes no token totals to Stats — those numbers aren't written anywhere Perch can read them after the fact. Its sessions, days and streaks all count normally, and Stats now says which agents a token total actually covers rather than quietly leaving one out.
